name: CLI Entry & Dispatch
description: The main bin/infernoflow.mjs router — parses argv, dispatches to command handlers, prints help, and silently records command usage for learning

name: AI Provider Router
description: Multi-tier AI provider abstraction — tries VS Code LM API, then Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/OpenRouter, then Ollama, then graceful fallback. Used by explain, why, review, changelog, suggest

name: AST Code Scanner
description: Deep static analysis of source files — extracts functions, external service calls, throws, internal calls, and maps them to capabilities. Writes inferno/scan.json

name: AI Capability Suggest
description: Builds a structured prompt from the current contract state, calls the AI provider, and applies the returned capability updates to capabilities.json

name: Contract Validator
description: Validates capabilities.json, scenarios, changelog, and contract shape. Exits non-zero on errors. Used as a CI gate and by watch mode

name: Dependency Graph Builder
description: Builds the capability dependency graph from capabilities.json call relationships. Writes inferno/graph.json with deps and dependents maps

name: Stability Management
description: freeze/thaw/stability commands — marks capabilities as frozen, stable, or experimental. Frozen caps trigger CRITICAL risk in impact analysis

name: Blast Radius Analysis
description: BFS traversal of the dependency graph to compute the blast radius of a capability change. Returns direct + transitive dependents and a risk level (low/medium/high/critical)

name: File-to-Capability Correlation
description: Given a source file or function name, finds the capability it belongs to using scan.json + graph.json. Shows stability, scenarios, git history, and blast radius

name: Project Initializer
description: Scaffolds inferno/ in a new or existing project. Detects language, framework, and project type. Supports --adopt mode for inferring capabilities from an existing codebase

name: Setup Wizard
description: One-command setup: detects IDE (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code), inits inferno/, installs git hooks, and configures MCP tools. The primary first-run experience

name: File Watcher
description: Watches source directories with fs.watch, debounces changes, checks capability relevance via capability-map.json, then runs suggest automatically. Writes issues to WATCH.log

name: AI Capability Narrative
description: Builds a structured prompt from capability context (stability, AST data, git history, scenarios, dependents) and calls AI to generate a 3-5 sentence human explanation. Falls back to structural summary

name: Capability Scaffolder
description: Generates a new source file skeleton + registers the capability in capabilities.json + writes a placeholder scenario. Detects project language and source directory automatically

name: Scenario Test Runner
description: Runs registered scenarios for capabilities. Auto-generates a smoke harness when no test runner is configured. Supports vitest, jest, mocha, and custom npm test scripts

name: AI Provider Manager
description: Interactive setup, status display, connection testing, and config clearing for AI providers. Writes to inferno/integrations.json. Supports anthropic, openai, gemini, openrouter, ollama

name: Interactive Demo
description: Self-contained 7-step narrated walkthrough: scaffolds a sample e-commerce project and runs stability, impact, explain, why, test, and CI gate in sequence

name: Local Web Dashboard
description: Express HTTP server on localhost:7337 with a live contract health view, capability list, agent runner, and Command Center for streaming CLI output to the browser

name: Developer Learning Layer
description: Silent command recorder (observe.mjs) + profile builder (profile.mjs) + pattern detector + skill synthesizer. Tracks usage patterns and suggests automatable workflows

name: AI Change Review
description: Reads git diff for staged or recent changes, identifies affected capabilities, and asks the AI provider for a concise impact summary. CI-friendly with --json output

name: Health Score
description: Computes a 0-100 health score across five dimensions: coverage, documentation, freshness, completeness, and drift. Provides actionable improvement recommendations

name: Setup Diagnostics
description: Diagnoses the infernoflow setup: checks Node version, git, contract integrity, AI provider config, MCP tool registration, and git hooks. Gives a clear pass/warn/fail for each check
